name: zsh-wordsplit-guard
description: Catches Bash commands that zsh, the Bash tool's shell, runs differently from bash. A loop over a bare expansion (`for x in $var`) runs once over the whole string, since zsh does not word-split it; a glob or a path around the expansion (`for f in $D/*.log`) is left alone. Also caught: an unquoted word or assignment value starting with `=` (`echo =====`, `[ a == b ]`, `v==x`), which zsh expands to a command path, and a glob in a `--flag=value` word (`--include=*.md`), which aborts on `no matches found` — both rewritten in place when the word is literal text, denied otherwise; and denied: parentheses in a `${var/pattern/…}` pattern, which zsh reads as a glob group; and bash's `${!name}` forms, which zsh aborts on or reads as `$!`. Each deny message names the form to use instead. The loop rule opts out per call with `[nosplit]` in the description, or session-wide with ALLOW_ZSH_NOSPLIT=1; the other rules opt out by the rewrite they apply or name.
